inspection_summary: Inspected all 4,808 normalized lines of Integral moments of L-functions. The source develops a quota-rich semantic chain: L-function structure and its characteristic-polynomial analogue; shifted moments as a desingularizing representation; a deliberately non-rigorous approximate-functional-equation/orthogonality recipe for all main terms; separation of universal polar factors from arithmetic Euler products; contour compression of permutation or sign sums; family-dependent symmetry selected by root numbers and coefficient averages; and numerical checks showing why lower-order terms matter. Formula extraction is often readable enough to locate the mechanism but exact symbolic reuse should be checked against the retained PDF.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, abstract, and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the full-main-term objective, the unitary/orthogonal/symplectic comparison, and the numerical-validation claim; the remainder is navigational front matter.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction and Statement of Results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates full moment polynomials and isolates the central heuristic tension between diagonal input and uncomputed off-diagonal cancellation.

sections_inspected.label: 1.1. Properties of L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the analytic, functional-equation, Euler-product, critical-line, conductor, and approximate-functional-equation structures used by the recipe.

sections_inspected.label: 1.2. Properties of characteristic polynomials
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds a representation-by-representation dictionary from L-functions to unitary characteristic polynomials and identifies matrix size with log conductor or local zero density.

sections_inspected.label: 1.3. Example families and moments of L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Classifies unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families and exhibits their distinct moment-polynomial degree laws and arithmetic/geometric leading factors.

sections_inspected.label: 1.4. Shifted moments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces shifted L/Z products and their random-matrix analogues as the representation in which pole structure and full moments become visible.

sections_inspected.label: 1.5. Main results and example conjectures
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Pairs full shifted L-function conjectures with exact compact-group formulas, using contour residues, Vandermonde factors, arithmetic Euler products, and refined conductors.

sections_inspected.label: 1.6. Second moment of the Riemann zeta-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Checks the recipe against Ingham's shifted second moment and exposes a nonvanishing residual constant under exponential smoothing.

sections_inspected.label: 1.7. Fourth moment of the Riemann zeta-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Matches the recipe's six shifted terms to Motohashi's residual main term and notes a lower-dimensional contour representation.

sections_inspected.label: 2 and 2.1. Moments in t-aspect and the recipe
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the six-step t-aspect recipe and explicitly records that discarded and restored main-sized terms are conjectured to cancel.

sections_inspected.label: 2.2. Moments of the Riemann zeta-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives nonoscillatory selection, diagonal extraction, the shifted Dirichlet series, and the permutation sum for zeta moments.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3. Moments of a primitive L-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers the zeta derivation to a general primitive L-function by Stirling analysis of functional-equation factors.

sections_inspected.label: 2.4. The arithmetic factor in the conjectures
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Factors the diagonal multiple Dirichlet series into its leading zeta poles and an analytic arithmetic Euler product.

sections_inspected.label: 2.5. Concise form of permutation sums
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves residue identities that compress singular permutation or sign sums into regular contour integrals and applies them to the general conjecture.

sections_inspected.label: 2.6. Explicit versions of the arithmetic factor
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Computes local arithmetic factors, shows the finite-zeta-product boundary at low moments, and establishes polynomial symmetry of local factors.

sections_inspected.label: 2.7. Recovering the leading order for moments of zeta
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recovers separately the arithmetic constant and random-matrix combinatorial constant in the previously conjectured leading coefficient.

sections_inspected.label: 3 and 3.1. Families of primitive characters
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines families through conductor ordering and multiplicative coefficient expectations, then derives orthogonality laws for t-twists, Dirichlet characters, quadratic characters, and newforms.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2. Families of L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs L-function families by Rankin-Selberg twisting and records the functional-equation regularity needed for a coherent family average.

sections_inspected.label: 4 and 4.1. General family recipe
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Generalizes the moment recipe to discrete families, with root-number expectations selecting terms and multiplicative coefficient averages producing Euler products and polar parts.

sections_inspected.label: 4.2. Unitary moments of a primitive L-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows t-aspect moments are a special case of the family formalism: phase averaging selects balanced terms and coefficient averaging selects diagonals.

sections_inspected.label: 4.3. Unitary family of primitive Dirichlet L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the unitary family analogue, with equality rather than congruence surviving in the limiting orthogonality relation and ramified primes omitted.

sections_inspected.label: 4.4. Quadratic twists of a real L-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives quadratic-twist moment terms and distinguishes symplectic from orthogonal symmetry by whether diagonal local coefficients contribute extra square factors and poles.

sections_inspected.label: 4.5. Cusp-form L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Petersson-weighted coefficient averages and root-number parity to conjecture orthogonal moments, including separate even/odd subfamilies.

sections_inspected.label: 5 and 5.1. Numerical zeta calculations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Computes full zeta moment polynomials and compares sharp and smoothed moments, demonstrating substantial lower-order contributions.

sections_inspected.label: 5.2. Quadratic Dirichlet calculations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Tests symplectic moment polynomials for both discriminant signs and explains shared fluctuations through rare large central values.

sections_inspected.label: 5.3. Orthogonal GL(2) twists
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Instantiates the orthogonal conjecture for conductor-11 elliptic-curve twists and uses a half-integral-weight modular-form identity as a computational bridge for central values.

sections_inspected.label: References, coefficient tables, and extracted figures
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Provides bibliography and numerical evidence tables; the final figure coordinate text is extraction-defective but its captions preserve the intended comparison.

accepted_units.title: Diagonal input, off-diagonal output, and the unexplained cancellation problem
accepted_units.why_material: The paper explicitly separates its simple diagonal recipe from the increasingly subtle off-diagonal contributions required by rigorous moment calculations. Its reusable insight is that a structurally correct final answer may arise from a deliberately incomplete detector only through conjectured cancellations that remain unexplained.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the contrast among low moments, higher-moment off-diagonals, symmetry-universal answers, and the warning in lines 145-151; severing the warning would misstate the recipe as a derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; no exact formula reconstruction is needed.

accepted_units.title: Primitive L-function structure, Z-normalization, log conductor, and approximate functional equation
accepted_units.why_material: This span assembles the semantic invariants later reused by every moment calculation: analytic continuation, functional-equation symmetry, Euler-product locality, primitive factorization, the critical point, zero density, a derivative-defined log conductor, and a two-piece approximate functional equation.
accepted_units.context_note: The Z-normalization matters because it makes the functional equation symmetric and critical-line values real; the conductor is chosen to match local zero density rather than merely repeat the usual arithmetic conductor.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mixed prose and displayed formulas; equation labels and prose are recoverable, but exact gamma-factor typography should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Characteristic-polynomial dictionary and conductor matching
accepted_units.why_material: The characteristic polynomial mirrors Dirichlet expansion, functional equation, critical locus, zero density, critical value, conductor, and a two-piece coefficient decomposition. Matching matrix size to L-function log conductor gives a concrete representation bridge, while the missing Euler product isolates arithmetic information.
accepted_units.context_note: Include the discussion through symmetry-type diagnostics: determinant/root-number behavior suggests but does not by itself determine the family symmetry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-supported analogy; exact polynomial identities are readable but scan verification is prudent for phase and conjugation notation.

accepted_units.title: Moment-polynomial degree laws across unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families
accepted_units.why_material: The examples expose a stable structural classification: moment degrees k squared, k(k+1)/2, and k(k-1)/2 accompany unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families, with leading coefficients split into arithmetic and compact-group factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The individual examples are conjectural except for stated low moments; use them as a comparative pattern, not as proved general laws.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual classification is prose-recoverable; exact Euler products and normalizations depend on displayed formulas.

accepted_units.title: Shifted moments expose structure and regularize coincident poles
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing an unshifted power by a product at independently shifted arguments makes the full mean-value structure visible and allows the original moment to be recovered by coalescing shifts. The same deformation has direct compact-group analogues.
accepted_units.context_note: Retain both continuous t-aspect and discrete-family definitions, since their parallel form is the bridge used later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent definitions, but the deformation-and-limit mechanism is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Full unitary moment conjecture as arithmetic deformation of an exact matrix integral
accepted_units.why_material: The contour-residue formula isolates matching pole geometry in zeta factors and characteristic-polynomial averages, with an additional analytic Euler product carrying arithmetic. Vandermonde cancellation explains polynomial degree, and equating zero densities explains the matrix-size/log-conductor substitution.
accepted_units.context_note: The L-function side is conjectural while the compact-group side is an exact quoted theorem; keep that epistemic distinction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; the prose validates pole locations and degree logic, but exact contour integrands require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Symplectic shifted moments and the refined conductor hidden in gamma factors
accepted_units.why_material: The quadratic-character conjecture and symplectic matrix theorem share sign-sum/contour structure. Re-expanding the functional-equation factor yields a refined conductor for which the first three leading polynomial terms become independent of residual gamma corrections, showing how a representation choice reorganizes lower-order terms.
accepted_units.context_note: The conductor comparison is source-specific and differs from the usual conductor by a significant constant/gamma contribution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy; the natural-conductor expansion and its O(z cubed) statement are prose-supported, while exact residues need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Orthogonal cusp-form moments, root-number sectors, and conductor normalization
accepted_units.why_material: The cusp-form conjecture pairs with SO and negative-determinant orthogonal averages, and the discussion shows how the functional-equation factor can be written as an exponential in a refined conductor times a cubic-order correction. Separate root-number sectors change the sign-weighted contour sum.
accepted_units.context_note: The harmonic Petersson weighting and squarefree-level assumptions are part of the claim; do not generalize to unweighted families without repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact normalization is formula-dependent and OCR-risky; the conductor and parity mechanism is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Second-moment calibration and a residual constant beyond the integrated main term
accepted_units.why_material: The k=1 residue recovers Ingham's shifted and unshifted second moment, while exponential smoothing leaves an explicit constant after subtracting the integrated conjectural main expression. This distinguishes asymptotic main-term agreement from exact finite residual behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: The smoothing theorem has uniformity conditions on shifts and the Laplace parameter; retain them for any exact use.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent, especially signs and limiting constants; verify exact equations against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Motohashi's fourth-moment decomposition matches the recipe's six balanced terms
accepted_units.why_material: An exact spectral formula decomposes the shifted fourth moment into a residual main term plus discrete, continuous, and holomorphic spectral pieces. After gamma-ratio asymptotics, its six residual terms match the recipe's balanced permutation terms, and a two-contour reformulation suggests nonminimality of the general four-contour representation.
accepted_units.context_note: Only the residual component is matched to the conjectured main term; the other spectral pieces are not claimed to vanish.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence and some extraction risk; term count and comparison are clear, exact Z-factor arguments need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Six-step t-aspect moment recipe with explicit non-rigorous failure modes
accepted_units.why_material: The procedure expands shifted approximate functional equations, retains nonoscillatory balanced terms, keeps diagonals, completes sums, and conjectures equality of averages. Crucially, the authors say the steps can discard and add terms of main-term size and are not individually justifiable.
accepted_units.context_note: Shifts are essential to avoid higher-order poles, and the completion step deliberately forgets original summation ranges.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Procedure is prose-grounded; displayed moment equality supplies the target but exact error typography should be checked.

accepted_units.title: Balanced phase selection produces the zeta permutation sum
accepted_units.why_material: For the shifted zeta product, Stirling phase analysis keeps exactly terms with equal numbers of opposing functional-equation factors. Diagonal extraction defines a multiple Dirichlet series, and symmetry compresses the survivors into choices of k shifts or ordered block permutations.
accepted_units.context_note: The Dirichlet series is initially divergent at the evaluation point and relies on later meromorphic continuation; keep that warning.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent; the nonoscillation criterion and combinatorial count are prose-supported, while exact exponents require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Transfer from zeta to a general primitive L-function
accepted_units.why_material: Under stated local-factor and gamma-factor assumptions, Stirling asymptotics again force an equal split between the two approximate-functional-equation pieces. The same diagonal and permutation architecture survives, with degree and gamma data entering only through the scale factor and arithmetic coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: The assumptions that gamma weights equal one half and local roots have modulus zero or one are conjectural for general arithmetic L-functions and must travel with the generalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; exact Q, degree, and exponent normalizations require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Diagonal Dirichlet series separates into universal zeta poles and an analytic arithmetic factor
accepted_units.why_material: Multiplicativity converts the constrained diagonal sum to an Euler product. Fourier integration enforces equality of exponent totals locally, the first-order local terms identify a product of zeta poles, and the remainder is analytic near the critical point, separating universal singular geometry from source-specific arithmetic.
accepted_units.context_note: Analyticity invokes assumed Ramanujan-type bounds and average size of prime coefficients; these are not unconditional for the full stated class.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The mechanism is recoverable from prose plus equation labels; exact local integrands are OCR-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Contour residues regularize singular permutation and sign sums
accepted_units.why_material: The lemmas turn sums over block permutations or all sign choices into Vandermonde-weighted contour integrals. Although individual summands have poles, the contour representation makes their cancellation and the regularity of the total transparent.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit includes the application to the general primitive-L moment, where the contour scale is identified with log conductor or mean zero density.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact residue powers and prefactors are formula-dependent; the cancellation mechanism is explicitly explained.

accepted_units.title: Explicit arithmetic factors, low-moment zeta products, and local polynomial symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: Residue evaluation gives closed local factors for degree-one Euler factors, identifies simple formulas for the first low moments, and marks a structural boundary: for k at least three the arithmetic factor cannot be a finite product of zeta-functions. A reversal symmetry shows each local factor is polynomial in both positive and negative shift monomials.
accepted_units.context_note: The long k=3 display is extraction-fragile; select the general lemma, boundary statement, and symmetry argument rather than trusting every printed coefficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High OCR/formula dependency; scan verification is mandatory before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Recovering the arithmetic leading constant from the full-moment Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: Scaling the contour variables isolates the highest power of log height. Evaluating the arithmetic factor at zero and reducing its local integral by residues and binomial identities reproduces the independently conjectured arithmetic constant a_k.
accepted_units.context_note: This is one half of the leading-coefficient factorization; the compact-group combinatorial constant is handled separately in the following unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent and extraction-sensitive, though the target identity and residue/binomial route are clear.

accepted_units.title: Recovering the random-matrix combinatorial constant by determinant transformations
accepted_units.why_material: Expanding Vandermonde determinants, exploiting block symmetry, converting contour coefficients to gamma reciprocals, and applying triangular determinant transformations reduces the remaining leading coefficient to the Keating-Snaith product g_k.
accepted_units.context_note: The conceptual determinant route is recoverable, but many matrix entries are visibly degraded in extraction; exact reconstruction must use the PDF.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Severe formula-layout dependency; accept only the prose-supported reduction mechanism pending scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Families as conductor-ordered coefficient systems with multiplicative expectations
accepted_units.why_material: A family is abstracted as arithmetic coefficient functions whose twists are primitive L-functions, ordered by a refined conductor, with limiting coefficient expectations required to exist and be multiplicative. This converts averaging into an Euler-product-producing orthogonality operator.
accepted_units.context_note: The definition is intentionally restrictive and parameterized; it should not be treated as a permanent ontology of all L-function families.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose and simple formulas; exact counting-function error exponents should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: t-twist and primitive-character averages collapse to exact diagonals
accepted_units.why_material: Continuous phase averaging yields equality of products as the surviving diagonal. Primitive-character averaging initially gives congruence modulo q, but with fixed inputs and q tending to infinity only exact equality persists, with a ramification coprimality condition.
accepted_units.context_note: The even and odd primitive characters form separate families under the paper's definition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-supported but robust; congruence-versus-equality distinction is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic-character orthogonality in restricted discriminant progressions
accepted_units.why_material: The average of a quadratic character vanishes unless the argument is a square up to primes constrained by the modulus, and the nonzero value is a product of local density corrections. Counting fundamental discriminants in progressions explains how sign, powers of two, common factors, and coprimality alter the local weights.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem imposes squarefreeness and 2-adic restrictions on the modulus; these conditions are essential.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several square glyphs are degraded to replacement characters, but the prose and cases recover the mechanism; exact statements require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Petersson weighting changes newform orthogonality and simplifies the moment detector
accepted_units.why_material: Hecke relations reduce products of eigenvalues to linear combinations. Unweighted and Petersson-weighted family averages select different coefficients; under Petersson weighting only the identity coefficient survives, and prime-power expectations become a Chebyshev/Sato-Tate integral whose multiplicativity feeds the Euler product.
accepted_units.context_note: The vanishing limit uses fixed indices and growth in weight or level, plus trace-formula bounds; it is not uniform without further work.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed trace and integral formulas are OCR-sensitive, while the weighting distinction and Chebyshev mechanism are prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Building L-function families by Rankin-Selberg twisting
accepted_units.why_material: A fixed primitive L-function is convolved locally with a family of character Euler factors, producing twisted coefficients and a required functional equation. Monotonic gamma data and separate treatment of finitely different archimedean types ensure that the resulting collection is coherent under conductor ordering.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction explicitly requires the twists to be L-functions; it does not infer analytic continuation from the formal Euler product.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-supported; local convolution indices and gamma parameters need scan verification for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: General family moment recipe and root-number symmetry selector
accepted_units.why_material: The t-aspect recipe is lifted to arbitrary families: expand two-piece functional equations, average root-number products, average coefficients, and complete sums. Expected root-number phases select balanced subsets differently for unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic families, while multiplicative coefficient expectations supply the surviving arithmetic series.
accepted_units.context_note: The source flags both the square-root choice for root numbers and the unexplained cancellation of ignored off-diagonal contributions; preserve both limitations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The selector counts and parity conditions are formula/prose recoverable; exact error normalization should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: From multiplicative family averages to symmetry-revealing polar products
accepted_units.why_material: Multiplicativity turns the completed average into local series. The first nonzero degree-two local terms determine whether zeta poles range over strict pairs or include diagonal pairs, leaving an analytic remainder and exposing the orthogonal-versus-symplectic degree pattern.
accepted_units.context_note: The source says this pole pattern is what usually occurs; family-specific coefficient averages must be checked before applying it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent but conceptually clear; exact local coefficient notation is extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: t-aspect moments are a unitary family average
accepted_units.why_material: Viewing n to the negative it as a character identifies a single L-function along the critical line with a family of twists. Averaging root-number phases becomes the nonoscillation rule, and averaging coefficients becomes diagonal selection, unifying the earlier recipe with the general family formalism.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an equivalence of the heuristic mechanisms under the stated definitions, not a proof of the moment conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded with simple functional-equation formulas.

accepted_units.title: Primitive Dirichlet families inherit the unitary moment architecture with ramified-prime repairs
accepted_units.why_material: Uniform root-number phases select balanced terms, while character orthogonality imposes product equality and coprimality to q. The resulting formulas match t-aspect unitary moments after omitting ramified Euler factors and retaining the appropriate archimedean X-factors.
accepted_units.context_note: Even and odd characters are averaged separately so that the functional-equation factor is constant within each family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-supported; exact X-factor substitutions require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic-twist symmetry is detected by the pole of the symmetric-square channel
accepted_units.why_material: Quadratic-character averaging forces products to be squares up to controlled ramified factors. Local expansion then always gives pairwise poles, while an additional diagonal pole appears precisely when the symmetric-square-type prime coefficient series has a pole; strict-pair poles yield orthogonal symmetry and diagonal-inclusive poles yield symplectic symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusion depends on primitivity assumptions, residue-class restrictions that freeze functional-equation data, and conjectural pole behavior for general L-functions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy with degraded square glyphs; the pole-order dichotomy is explicit in prose, exact local products need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Orthogonal cusp-form moments from Petersson averages and root-number parity
accepted_units.why_material: For newform L-functions, random root-number signs keep only parity-compatible approximate-functional-equation terms, and Petersson-weighted coefficient averages produce the arithmetic Euler product. Sign-restricted sums then separate even and odd subfamilies and contour compression recovers the stated orthogonal conjecture.
accepted_units.context_note: The harmonic weighting is integral to the derivation, and the even/odd projections should not be conflated with the combined family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence; exact sign products and X-factor placement require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Full zeta polynomials show lower-order dominance at accessible heights
accepted_units.why_material: Explicit and numerical moment polynomials reveal that leading coefficients can be far smaller than lower-order coefficients and that coefficient signs eventually vary. Sharp-block and exponential-weight comparisons agree closely with the full polynomial, illustrating why leading-order-only validation would be misleading.
accepted_units.context_note: The data support the conjecture and stated error scale but do not prove either; numerical coefficient precision varies with moment order.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Large formulas and decimals are extraction-readable but should be machine-checked against source tables before quantitative reuse.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic-family checks separate discriminant signs and expose rare-value skew
accepted_units.why_material: Moment polynomials are computed separately for positive and negative discriminants and compared under a frozen smooth cutoff. Similar fluctuations across moment orders are traced to rare large central values whose influence grows with k, identifying a concrete heavy-tail confound in moment validation.
accepted_units.context_note: The numerical evidence is family- and cutoff-specific; the approximate-functional-equation implementation is only briefly described.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; exact cutoff function and table values are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Orthogonal GL(2) twist test via a half-integral-weight modular form
accepted_units.why_material: For the conductor-11 elliptic-curve L-function, residue classes select twists with even functional equation, the conjecture supplies a degree k(k-1)/2 moment polynomial, and a Kohnen-Zagier relation converts central values into squared coefficients of an explicit weight-3/2 form, enabling a large exact-data comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: The arithmetic-factor coefficients were computed at low precision, so agreement is limited by coefficient accuracy; the modular-form identity applies only to the specified fundamental discriminants.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact Euler factors, theta-series congruence conditions, and normalization constant are formula-dependent and should be verified against the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Log conductor as the invariant bridge between analytic and matrix representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across t-aspect and discrete families, differentiating the functional-equation factor at the critical point packages local zero density into a scale that matches matrix size; re-expanding around this scale relocates archimedean corrections into lower polynomial coefficients.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The matrix correspondence is heuristic on the L-function side, and exact conductor normalizations are family-specific.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Shifts turn singular moment powers into a tractable deformation calculus
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Independent shifts avoid coincident higher-order poles, label the balanced functional-equation choices, expose singular factors, and permit contour identities whose regular coalescing limit recovers the unshifted moment.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Analytic continuation and cancellation justify the representation only formally within the conjectural recipe; coalescing limits need exact pole control.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A deliberately lossy detector can predict a full answer only through a cancellation hypothesis
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Phase or root-number averaging selects balanced approximate-functional-equation pieces and coefficient averaging selects diagonals, producing the observed compact formula even though rigorous analyses contain main-sized off-diagonal terms; the recipe therefore encodes a structural cancellation conjecture, not a proof heuristic.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Agreement in known cases and numerics does not identify or prove the missing cancellation mechanism.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Universal pole geometry and arithmetic local data are separable layers
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Multiplicative diagonal averages factor into zeta-like poles that determine degree and symmetry plus an analytic Euler product that records arithmetic and supplies the leading constant at zero shift.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The analytic remainder and prime-coefficient bounds rely on stated or conjectural assumptions, and higher-moment arithmetic factors no longer reduce to finite zeta products.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Family symmetry is an output of averaging laws, not merely a root-number label
